we propose a novel low-rank matrix recovery problem with missing entries and unknown correspondence, and develop a new algorithm to solve it.

we propose a novel matrix recovery problem with an unknown correspondence among heterogeneous data and propose a provably convergent algorithm, $\textbf{M}^{3}\textbf{O}$, that solves the problem.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, by leveraging the low-rank property of the underlying data, one can recover the unknown correspondence among heterogeneous data without knowing it.

the nuclear norm minimization is a robust tool to recover the low-rank matrix from a partial observation with unknown correspondence, and it can be solved efficiently by a proximal gradient algorithm with a Max- Oracle.

it is possible, in theory and in practice, to recover low-rank data matrices from heterogeneous observations with unknown correspondence, and the recovery can be done by a simple and efficient algorithm.
